title: Output quantisation changes reconstruction effectiveness but is not assumed secure

invariants.description: On the same targets, 4-bucket quantisation must reduce correct reconstructions (observed 7/200 = 3.5 points, McNemar p = 0.0078; positive on 20/20 seeds but significant at 0.05 on only 7/20, so significance is NOT asserted).
A NEW attack against the quantised service must still beat the auxiliary-only attacker by ≥ 20 points (observed +55/200 = +27.5%; 20-seed min +24.0). Quantisation is not a privacy guarantee.
Leakage under quantisation must remain significant (observed p = 2.8e-17).
Quantisation must not cost decision accuracy (observed 301/400 = 75.25%, identical to full probability on 20/20 seeds).

rationale: Bucket width 0.25 only hides the attribute when both candidate scores fall into the same bucket; the attribute shifts the score by more than that for most records. The effect is real but small and seed-dependent.
